stimuli.text: Directions (76-80): Read the following passage carefully and  fill in the blanks with the most appropriate word from the given alternatives. In an age increasingly enamored of instantaneous information, intellectual restraint has become an almost antiquated virtue. The contemporary reader is perpetually assailed by a prodigious volume of claims, conjectures, and polemics, many of which acquire an unwarranted aura of credibility merely through repetition. What is particularly disquieting is not the sheer abundance of information but the gradual erosion of the cognitive habits required to interrogate it. A proposition that ought to invite scrutiny is instead accepted with remarkable alacrity, while evidence that complicates an established conviction is frequently dismissed as an inconvenient (1)________. This tendency is exacerbated by digital platforms whose algorithms are designed less to cultivate discernment than  to maximise engagement. By continuously presenting users with material consonant with their pre-existing preferences, such systems can create an epistemic environment that is deceptively (2)________. Within such an environment, disagreement is no longer perceived as an opportunity for intellectual refinement but as an affront to one’s identity. Consequently, individuals become increasingly (3)________ to information that unsettles their assumptions, even when such information is supported by cogent evidence. The predicament is further complicated by the proliferation of ostensibly authoritative voices whose expertise is difficult to verify. Eloquence, confidence, and rhetorical dexterity are often mistaken for substantive knowledge, allowing specious arguments to acquire an appearance of legitimacy. The resulting confusion is not merely (4)________; it can have tangible consequences when poorly examined claims influence public policy, medical decisions, or collective perceptions of social reality. The remedy, therefore, cannot consist simply in accumulating more information. What is required is a deliberate cultivation of intellectual habits that enable individuals to distinguish the plausible from the demonstrable, the persuasive from the (5)________, and the familiar from the genuinely verifiable. In an informational ecosystem increasingly saturated with noise, scepticism—properly understood not as cynical disbelief but as disciplined inquiry—may be among the most indispensable forms of intellectual hygiene.
